chapter.title: Pulp of Wood or of Other Fibrous Cellulosic Material; Recovered (Waste and Scrap) Paper or Paperboard

page.h1: HTS Chapter 47: Pulp of Wood or of Other Fibrous Cellulosic Material; Recovered (Waste and Scrap) Paper or Paperboard — U.S. Exports & Foreign Tariffs

seo.title: U.S. Wood Pulp, Fluff Pulp & OCC Exports by Country (HTS Ch. 47) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: U.S. pulp and waste paper exports were $7.99B in 2025, down 6.3%. Fluff and kraft pulp, OCC, who buys them now that China bans waste paper, and what they pay.

intro:
The U.S. exported **$7.99B** of wood pulp and recovered paper in 2025, down 6.3% on 2024 and 26% below the 2022 peak ($10.85B). Kraft pulp (4703) is **60%** of it ($4.81B), almost all bleached softwood kraft, the line that includes the fluff pulp used in diapers and other absorbent products (4703.21, **$4.33B**). Recovered paper (4707: waste paper, old corrugated containers or OCC, mixed paper) adds **$2.28B**, led by OCC (4707.10, $1.52B), and dissolving pulp (4702) $725M. **China ($996M, down 21.1%) and Mexico ($983M)** are the largest buyers, followed by India, Japan, Canada, Thailand, Viet Nam, Indonesia and Malaysia.

Tariffs are low: the EU, Japan, Mexico, Canada, Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia charge 0% on U.S. pulp and recovered paper, and India charges 5% on pulp and 2.5% on recovered paper. Two buyers charge more. **China** adds a 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods, plus 5% on wood pulp under its 2018 counter-tariff list unless the buyer holds an exclusion, and **Canada** has charged a 50% surtax on U.S. dissolving pulp since September 8, 2026. For recovered paper the buyer's import rules matter more than the tariff: **China has banned all solid-waste imports, recovered paper included, since January 1, 2021** (it bought $4M of U.S. recovered paper in 2025), so U.S. OCC now goes to India, Mexico, Thailand, Viet Nam and Malaysia, which license or inspect scrap paper shipments. In the EU, deforestation due diligence applies to wood pulp from December 30, 2026.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.
keyTakeaways: U.S. Chapter 47 exports fell 6.3% to $7.99B in 2025 and another 7.2% in January–August 2026 ($4.94B); bleached softwood kraft pulp, which includes fluff pulp (4703.21, $4.33B), and OCC (4707.10, $1.52B) are the two largest lines.

China is still the largest buyer ($996M) but takes almost only pulp ($773M of kraft pulp, $211M of dissolving pulp): its solid-waste import ban has kept out U.S. recovered paper since January 1, 2021. U.S. pulp pays 10% there, or 15% for buyers without an exclusion; watch December 31, 2026 and January 10, 2027.

U.S. recovered paper ($2.28B) now goes mainly to India ($369M), Mexico ($368M), Thailand ($354M), Viet Nam ($314M) and Malaysia ($294M), which charge 0–2.5%; meeting each buyer's licence, inspection and contamination rules decides whether a container clears.

Canada's 50% surtax since September 8, 2026 reaches only dissolving pulp (U.S. sales there were $62,000 in 2025); kraft pulp, fluff pulp and recovered paper enter Canada free. The EU charges 0% but requires deforestation due-diligence statements for wood pulp from December 30, 2026.
